items.description: Are audit and assurance policies and procedures established, documented, approved, communicated, applied, evaluated, and maintained?
Are independent audit and assurance assessments conducted in accordance with relevant standards at least annually?
Is a risk-based audit and assurance assessment plan developed, approved, and executed across all cloud services?
Are audit trails, activity logs, and evidence records protected against unauthorized access, tampering, or deletion?
Is a formal audit management process established to track audit findings, exceptions, and corrective action plans?
Are audit and assurance deficiencies remediated within established timeframes according to identified risk severity?
Are application and interface security policies and procedures established, documented, approved, communicated, applied, evaluated, and maintained?
Are baseline security requirements established, documented, and maintained for all applications across the software development lifecycle?
Are application security metrics established, monitored, and reported to evaluate the effectiveness of application security controls?
Are secure architecture, design, and coding practices (e.g. threat modeling, OWASP Top 10) integrated into the application development process?
Is automated static (SAST) and dynamic (DAST) application security testing integrated into the automated continuous deployment pipeline?
Are automated integrity checks, code signing, and release validation enforced prior to deploying applications to production?
Are application security flaws, design vulnerabilities, and software defects remediated within defined SLAs based on severity?

items.category: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
items.description: Are business continuity management and operational resilience policies and procedures established, documented, approved, communicated, applied, evaluated, and maintained?

items.category: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
items.description: Are business impact analyses (BIA) and operational risk assessments conducted periodically to determine critical services, RTOs, and RPOs?

items.category: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
items.description: Is an enterprise business continuity strategy documented and approved that accounts for multi-region failover and critical service dependencies?

items.category: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
items.description: Are comprehensive business continuity plans documented, maintained, and readily accessible during operational disruptions?

items.category: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
items.description: Are technical disaster recovery plans established with defined Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO)?

items.category: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
items.description: Are business continuity and disaster recovery plans exercised and tested at least annually via tabletop and failover simulations?

items.category: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
items.description: Are internal and external emergency communication procedures established to notify personnel, customers, and authorities during critical outages?

items.category: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
items.description: Are automated backups performed, encrypted, and replicated to geographically distinct locations with immutable retention policies?

items.category: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
items.description: Are backup restoration procedures tested and validated regularly to ensure recovery capability within agreed RTOs?

items.category: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
items.description: Is critical cloud infrastructure deployed with high-availability configurations, redundant components, and automated failover?

items.category: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
items.description: Are redundant power feeds, uninterruptible power supply (UPS) batteries, and backup generators maintained and tested regularly?
Are change control and configuration management policies and procedures established, documented, approved, communicated, applied, evaluated, and maintained?
Are automated mechanisms deployed to continuously detect, alert on, and remediate unauthorized configuration changes or drift?
Are changes to cloud infrastructure and software managed through automated Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) and CI/CD pipelines?
Are development, testing, staging, and production environments physically or logically segregated with strict promotion gates?
Are production releases, schema migrations, and configuration updates peer-reviewed and formally approved prior to execution?
Are hardened baseline configuration standards (e.g. CIS Benchmarks) established, documented, and maintained for all system components?
Is configuration drift continuously monitored and automatically reconciled against approved baseline configurations?
Are emergency change governance procedures defined, documented, and audited with post-implementation verification and sign-off?
Are rollback and restoration procedures documented, automated, and tested for all production releases and infrastructure deployments?
Are cryptography, encryption, and key management policies and procedures established, documented, approved, communicated, applied, evaluated, and maintained?
Are cryptographic management roles, access authorizations, and operational responsibilities clearly segregated and defined?
Is sensitive and customer data encrypted at rest using industry-standard algorithms (e.g. AES-256) across all storage tiers?
Is data in transit encrypted using modern TLS protocols (TLS 1.3 preferred, TLS 1.2 minimum) with strong cipher suites?
Are cryptographic algorithms, modes, and cipher suites aligned with NIST FIPS standards, prohibiting broken or deprecated ciphers?
Are master cryptographic keys generated, stored, and managed in FIPS 140-2/3 Level 3 validated Hardware Security Modules (HSM)?
Are cryptographic keys generated using approved cryptographically secure pseudorandom number generators (CSPRNG)?
Are capabilities provided for cloud service customers to manage, supply, and control their own encryption keys (BYOK / HYOK)?
Are cryptographic keys rotated automatically on defined schedules (at least annually) and upon role change or suspected compromise?
Are formal procedures and automated mechanisms implemented to securely revoke and zeroize compromised or retired keys?
Are data encryption keys separated from key encryption keys (envelope encryption) with access governed by distinct IAM policies?
Is access to cryptographic keys restricted based on the principle of least privilege, strict IAM roles, and multi-party authorization?
Are secure key backup, escrow, and recovery procedures implemented to prevent permanent data loss in disaster scenarios?
Are digital certificates automatically tracked, renewed, and deployed prior to expiration using centralized lifecycle automation?
Is public key infrastructure (PKI) rooted in trusted, audited internal or public Certificate Authorities (CAs)?
Are all cryptographic key generation, rotation, access, export, and destruction events logged to an immutable audit trail?
Are cryptographic systems regularly audited to detect and sunset deprecated protocols, hash functions (SHA-1/MD5), and weak ciphers?
Is an organizational strategy established to evaluate and adopt post-quantum cryptographic standards (PQC) across sensitive assets?
Is application-layer field-level encryption applied to highly confidential data elements prior to database persistence?
Are key compromise emergency response procedures documented and tested to re-encrypt data and rotate compromised keys rapidly?
Are key export and migration capabilities governed by strict envelope encryption standards preventing plaintext key exposure?
Are datacenter physical and environmental security policies and procedures established, documented, approved, communicated, applied, evaluated, and maintained?
Are decommissioned storage devices and hardware sanitized, degaussed, or physically destroyed according to NIST SP 800-88 standards?
Are hardware and storage media movements between datacenter locations tracked with chain-of-custody documentation and physical security?
Is datacenter equipment serviced and maintained only by authorized personnel in accordance with manufacturer specifications?
Are physical and virtual assets classified according to their criticality, sensitivity, and operational value?
Is an accurate, comprehensive, and automated physical asset inventory maintained covering all datacenter hardware and network gear?
Are physical access points secured with perimeter fencing, security guards, anti-passback turnstiles, and biometric access controls?
Is 24/7 closed-circuit television (CCTV) monitoring and recording maintained at all facility perimeters, access points, and server rooms with 90-day retention?
Are all datacenter visitors logged, authenticated with government ID, badged, and escorted by authorized personnel at all times?
Are climate control systems (HVAC) continuously monitored to maintain temperature, humidity, and airflow within equipment tolerances?
Are early warning smoke detection and clean-agent fire suppression systems deployed and inspected regularly across datacenter rooms?
Are redundant utility power feeds, uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), and emergency backup diesel generators with onsite fuel reserves maintained?
Are telecommunication and electrical power cables protected from physical interception, accidental damage, and electromagnetic interference?
Are datacenters constructed in locations assessed for low risk of seismic activity, flooding, hurricanes, and geological hazards?
Are physical storage media transported via secure couriers with tamper-evident packaging and real-time tracking?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Are data security, privacy lifecycle management, and personal data protection policies and procedures established, documented, approved, communicated, applied, evaluated, and maintained?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Is a formal privacy compliance framework implemented adhering to GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, and applicable global privacy mandates?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Is an inventory of all customer data, personal information (PII), and sensitive corporate data mapped and maintained across cloud repositories?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Is a formal data classification taxonomy (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) applied and enforced across all cloud data stores?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Are end-to-end data flows documented illustrating ingestion, processing, storage, transit, and cross-border transfer paths?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Are data owners and stewards designated and held accountable for managing access, classification, and protection of data assets?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Are data retention, archiving, and disposal schedules enforced in accordance with statutory, contractual, and business requirements?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Are customer tenant data and backups permanently deleted and cryptographically scrubbed upon account termination or deletion requests?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Is production personal and sensitive data strictly prohibited or masked/pseudonymized before use in development and test environments?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Is access to customer and sensitive data restricted strictly based on business need-to-know, role authorization, and tenant context?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Are automated Data Loss Prevention (DLP) controls deployed across cloud storage, email, endpoints, and APIs to block unauthorized egress?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Are privacy-by-design and data minimization principles integrated into service architectures to collect only necessary data?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Are international and cross-border data transfers governed by standard contractual clauses (SCCs) and regulatory safeguards?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Are automated mechanisms provided to honor data subject access, rectification, portability, and deletion requests (GDPR DSAR)?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Are technical capabilities implemented to place immutable legal holds on relevant tenant data during litigation or regulatory inquiries?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Are customers notified of any cloud sub-processors with access to customer data prior to authorization and onboarding?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Are privacy incident protocols documented detailing immediate containment, forensic root-cause analysis, and regulatory breach notification?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Is multi-tenant customer data logically separated with strict database partitioning and access control filters preventing cross-tenant leakage?

items.category: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
items.description: Are physical and logical geographic storage regions of customer data documented and transparently disclosed to customers?
Does the organization maintain a formal Information Security Governance Program with executive leadership and Board oversight?
Is a certified Information Security Management System (ISMS) (e.g. ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2 Type II) maintained and reviewed annually?
Is a comprehensive enterprise risk management framework implemented to identify, analyze, evaluate, and treat organizational risks?
Is an enterprise risk register maintained with designated risk owners, mitigation deadlines, and residual risk acceptance records?
Are organizational security policies published, communicated to all personnel, and formally reviewed at least annually?
Are legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual cloud compliance requirements identified, documented, and continuously tracked?
Are cloud information systems mapped against relevant regulatory standards to demonstrate compliance coverage and control alignment?
Is a formal security policy exception process established requiring documented justification, compensating controls, and executive sign-off?
Are background checks and identity verification conducted for all prospective employees and contractors prior to employment?
Is an Acceptable Use Policy documented, communicated, and formally acknowledged by all personnel accessing organizational assets?
Are clean desk and clear screen policies enforced across all office environments and remote work settings?
Do employment contracts and agreements include legally binding confidentiality, intellectual property, and nondisclosure commitments?
Are all corporate assets, cryptographic hardware, and credentials returned and accounted for upon employment termination or role transition?
Are automated deprovisioning procedures executed immediately upon employee termination to revoke all physical and logical access?
Do all employees complete mandatory security and privacy awareness training upon hire and at least annually thereafter?
Are software developers and engineers trained regularly in secure application design, secure coding practices, and OWASP vulnerabilities?
Are privileged users and system administrators trained in administrative security, least privilege, and audited operational duties?
Is a formal disciplinary process established, communicated, and enforced for personnel who commit security policy violations?
Are security guidelines, VPN/ZTNA requirements, and secure home office standards established for remote and mobile workers?
Are third-party contractors and temporary staff subjected to background verification and contractual security obligations equal to employees?
Are personnel clearly instructed on how to report suspected security incidents, phishing attempts, and compliance violations without reprisal?
Are identity and access management policies and procedures established, documented, approved, communicated, applied, evaluated, and maintained?
Are unique user identities assigned to each individual, with shared or generic accounts strictly prohibited?
Is phishing-resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA/FIDO2) enforced for all administrative and user access to cloud systems?
Are modern credential standards (passkeys, NIST SP 800-63B password rules, breach database checks) enforced?
Are administrative access privileges provisioned just-in-time (JIT) with automated expiration and dual authorization?
Are inactive user sessions automatically terminated after a defined period, requiring re-authentication to resume access?
Are duties segregated to prevent a single individual from initiating, approving, and executing critical actions or deployments?
Are long-lived service account keys prohibited in favor of short-lived workload identity federation (OIDC / IAM Roles)?
Are user access permissions and privileged roles reviewed and recertified by asset owners at least quarterly?
Are user access privileges revoked or updated within 24 hours of role change, reassignment, or employment termination?
Is cloud customer approval required before cloud provider personnel can access customer tenant data or environments?
Are cloud services integrated with enterprise identity providers via standard SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect (OIDC) protocols?
Are API keys, tokens, and operational secrets stored in secure secret vaults with automated rotation and access logging?
Is access to cloud resources governed by granular Role-Based (RBAC) and Attribute-Based (ABAC) least-privilege policies?
Are privileged administrative sessions recorded, keystroke-logged, and monitored in real time for unauthorized activities?
Are context-aware, zero-trust authorization policies enforced taking device health, location, and risk scores into account?
Are open, well-documented, standardized APIs provided to allow seamless interoperability between customer systems and cloud services?
Are API specifications, versioning roadmaps, and deprecation schedules published to ensure service continuity for consumers?
Are cloud workloads packaged using open standards (e.g. OCI container images) to facilitate migration between cloud providers?
Are contractual agreements and documented procedures established allowing customers to export all tenant data in standard formats upon exit?
Are infrastructure and virtualization security policies and procedures established, documented, approved, communicated, applied, evaluated, and maintained?
Are system compute, storage, and network capacities monitored and planned to ensure adequate headroom during peak workloads?
Are cloud networks segmented using Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs), network security groups, firewalls, and micro-segmentation?
Are hypervisors and virtualization hosts hardened according to industry benchmarks with unnecessary drivers and services disabled?
Are operating systems and base container images hardened according to CIS Benchmarks and verified by automated configuration scanners?
Are multi-tenant compute workloads isolated using hardware-enforced virtualization boundaries or secure container runtimes?
Is direct SSH/RDP access to production hosts disabled from the Internet and replaced with session-monitored bastion/systems managers?
Are container images scanned for vulnerabilities in registries and cryptographically signed (e.g. Cosign) before deployment?
Are admission controllers (e.g. OPA Gatekeeper/Kyverno) and runtime security agents active on container clusters to block unapproved workloads?
Are security logging, event correlation, and system monitoring policies and procedures established, documented, approved, communicated, applied, evaluated, and maintained?
Are audit logs protected against unauthorized modification, tampering, or deletion using immutable, append-only storage?
Are security events, authentication attempts, privilege escalations, system errors, and access changes logged across all cloud services?
Is access to audit logs restricted strictly to authorized security personnel, with all access to log records logged and audited?
Are audit logs ingested into a centralized SIEM/SOAR system with automated real-time correlation and incident alerting rules?
Are internal system clocks across all servers and network devices synchronized to an authenticated Network Time Protocol (NTP) time source?
Are audit and security logs retained for a minimum of 12 months (or as required by statutory regulations) with at least 90 days immediately searchable?
Is a centralized SIEM platform deployed to aggregate telemetry across cloud infrastructure, SaaS endpoints, and container runtimes?
Are network traffic metadata and VPC flow logs captured and analyzed continuously to detect anomalous network connections?
Are all privileged user actions, root activities, and cloud console administrative operations logged with user attribution?
Are capabilities provided for customers to export or stream raw security event logs directly into their own SIEM systems?
Are all authorization decisions, policy changes, and permission assignments logged and reviewed periodically?

items.category: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
items.description: Are security incident management, e-discovery, and cloud forensics policies and procedures established, documented, approved, communicated, applied, evaluated, and maintained?

items.category: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
items.description: Is an incident response plan with technical playbooks documented covering ransomware, data breach, denial of service, and insider threat?

items.category: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
items.description: Is a dedicated, trained Incident Response Team or 24/7 Managed Detection and Response (MDR) provider operational and contactable?

items.category: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
items.description: Are incident response procedures tested at least annually via tabletop exercises, red team simulations, and purple team evaluations?

items.category: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
items.description: Are incident escalation procedures established to notify affected customers and statutory regulators within statutory deadlines (e.g. 72 hours)?

items.category: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
items.description: Are security incidents triaged and classified according to standard severity taxonomies to guide response prioritization?

items.category: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
items.description: Are forensic collection capabilities enabled to snapshot disk volumes, capture volatile RAM, and preserve forensic artifacts without altering system state?

items.category: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
items.description: Are formal post-incident reviews conducted to identify root causes, establish corrective action plans, and track remediation to completion?

items.category: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
items.description: Are supply chain risk management, vendor evaluation, and third-party transparency policies and procedures established, documented, approved, communicated, applied, evaluated, and maintained?

items.category: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
items.description: Are third-party vendor risk assessments conducted prior to contracting and re-evaluated at least annually for all active suppliers?

items.category: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
items.description: Is a comprehensive list of all external sub-processors and cloud suppliers published and accessible to customers?

items.category: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
items.description: Do vendor contracts mandate adherence to enterprise security standards, data protection terms, and agreed operational SLAs?

items.category: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
items.description: Do supplier agreements grant the right to conduct security audits or require annual independent SOC 2 / ISO 27001 certifications?

items.category: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
items.description: Are suppliers contractually obligated to report security incidents affecting customer data within predefined emergency timeframes?

items.category: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
items.description: Are open-source software packages scanned for license compliance and security vulnerabilities before incorporation into production builds?

items.category: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
items.description: Are Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) generated and maintained for all software releases to track software component provenance?

items.category: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
items.description: Are vulnerabilities in third-party libraries and container dependencies tracked and patched according to severity SLAs?

items.category: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
items.description: Is supplier security posture continuously monitored using third-party security rating services and compliance audit alerts?

items.category: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
items.description: Are internal controls periodically tested to verify ongoing compliance with upstream customer and partner security requirements?

items.category: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
items.description: Are formal offboarding procedures implemented to ensure suppliers securely return or destroy all proprietary data upon contract termination?

items.category: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
items.description: Are risks arising from supplier geographical location, legal jurisdiction, and geopolitical instability assessed and mitigated?

items.category: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
items.description: Are server hardware and network components acquired from vetted suppliers with verified cryptographic signatures and tamper-evident packaging?
Are threat and vulnerability management policies and procedures established, documented, approved, communicated, applied, evaluated, and maintained?
Are automated vulnerability scans conducted weekly across all cloud infrastructure, network endpoints, and operating systems?
Are critical vulnerabilities remediated within 14 days and high vulnerabilities within 30 days of discovery in accordance with defined SLAs?
Is an external penetration test performed at least annually by an independent accredited offensive security firm?
Is threat intelligence integrated into defensive operations and architectural threat models to proactively counter emerging adversary tactics?
Is a public vulnerability disclosure policy (security.txt) or bug bounty program maintained for external security researchers?
Are security patches for operating systems, hypervisors, and software applications tested and deployed automatically within maintenance windows?
Are compensating controls (such as WAF virtual patching, network isolation) deployed when vendor patches cannot be immediately applied?
Is the external attack surface continuously mapped and monitored to identify rogue cloud assets, exposed ports, and shadow IT?
Are Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) agents active across all cloud compute instances and server workloads with automated quarantine?
Are expedited zero-day vulnerability response protocols established to assess exposure and apply workarounds within 24 hours of notification?
Are production web applications and APIs protected by an enterprise WAAP/WAF solution inspecting ingress traffic for OWASP threats?
Are vulnerability remediation exceptions documented with expiration dates, business justifications, and executive approval?
Are universal endpoint management, mobile device security, and client workstation policies and procedures established, documented, approved, communicated, applied, evaluated, and maintained?
Is application allowlisting or centralized software catalog enforcement deployed to prevent the execution of unapproved software on endpoints?
Are endpoint health posture checks enforced to verify OS compliance, antivirus status, and firewall status before granting network access?
Are endpoint operating systems and client software patched automatically within 30 days of vendor release?
Is full disk encryption (e.g. BitLocker, FileVault) enforced on all laptops and workstations with centralized recovery key escrow?
Are endpoints configured to automatically lock screens and require password/biometric re-entry after 15 minutes of inactivity?
Are all corporate and BYOD endpoints enrolled in a centralized Mobile Device Management (MDM) / Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) solution?
Are administrative privileges restricted on endpoints, blocking local users from executing unauthorized scripts or disabling security tools?
Are centralized, behavior-based EDR agents installed on all corporate endpoints with real-time telemetry and isolation capabilities?
Are jailbroken or rooted mobile devices automatically detected and blocked from accessing corporate cloud systems and email?
Are endpoint DLP controls active to prevent unauthorized copying of sensitive corporate data to unencrypted local storage or personal cloud apps?
Are USB mass storage devices and removable media blocked or restricted to encrypted corporate drives on all endpoints?
